quizName: DMV Practice Test #9 30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: What should a proper lane position do?

options.text: Help you see better and be seen by others.
Place you in other drivers' blind spots.
Encourage other drivers to share your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help you see better and be seen by others.
questions.explanation: Good lane position helps you see other drivers and lets them see you. It helps you avoid wind blasts, blind spots, and road hazards. It also stops other drivers from trying to share your lane and gives you an escape route if danger appears.

questions.question: What helps other drivers see your motorcycle?

options.text: Make eye contact with other drivers.

questions.explanation: Using your headlight is the best way to help other drivers see your motorcycle. Always check that your headlight works before you ride.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. They warn you about upcoming road conditions. This sign means the road ahead is divided.

questions.question: What does a solid red arrow on a traffic signal mean?

options.text: You may go through with caution.

questions.explanation: A solid red arrow means the same as a red light. You must stop completely and wait for a green light before turning in that direction.

questions.question: When does a motorcycle have less traction for braking?

options.text: When the motorcycle is straight up and down.

questions.explanation: When a motorcycle leans during a turn, there is less traction for braking. You can use both brakes while turning, but you must be very careful.

questions.question: Which lane position makes a motorcyclist most visible?
questions.explanation: The center lane position is usually best when following a car because the driver can see you in their rearview mirror. Be ready to change positions if traffic or road conditions change.

questions.question: How can you reduce the chance of a crash?
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, be visible, signal your moves, keep safe distance, look 12 seconds ahead, spot hazards early, and be ready for changing conditions.

questions.question: What should you do when it starts to rain?

options.text: Ride on the right side of the lane.
Ride on the edge of the road.
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: When it first rains, the road is very slippery. Rainwater mixes with oil left by cars. Ride in the tire tracks where other cars have already passed.

questions.question: If another driver makes eye contact with you, what does it mean?

options.text: It doesn't always mean they've seen you.

questions.correctAnswerText: It doesn't always mean they've seen you.
questions.explanation: Never assume that eye contact means a driver has seen you. Drivers often look directly at motorcycles but still don't notice them.

questions.question: Who can operate a motorized scooter?

options.text: Anyone with any class of driver license.

questions.correctAnswerText: Anyone with any class of driver license.
questions.explanation: In California, anyone with any type of driver license can operate a motorized scooter.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead. This sign warns that the road will be slippery when it is wet.

questions.question: Under normal conditions, a motorcyclist should keep a following distance of at least:
questions.explanation: Keep at least two seconds between you and the vehicle ahead under normal conditions. In poor conditions, increase this distance.

questions.question: When approaching an intersection, a motorcyclist should NOT:

options.text: Choose a lane position that makes them more visible.
Speed up to cross the intersection quickly.
Cover the clutch and brakes to be ready to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up to cross the intersection quickly.
questions.explanation: Choose a lane position that other drivers can see you in. Cover your clutch and brakes so you can stop quickly. Slow down as you approach an intersection. Do not suddenly change your speed or position, as this may confuse other drivers.

questions.question: If another vehicle is passing you, you should:

options.text: Ride on the left side of your lane.
Ride in the center of your lane.
Ride on the right side of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center of your lane.
questions.explanation: The center of your lane is the safest position when being passed. Riding on the side closest to the passing vehicle risks a crash. Riding on the far side may make the other driver return to your lane too soon.

questions.question: A good lane position should:

options.text: Help you see others and be seen.
Place you in other drivers' blind spots.
Allow others to share your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help you see others and be seen.
questions.explanation: Choose a lane position that helps you see others and helps them see you. It should keep you away from blind spots and surface hazards. It should discourage others from sharing your lane and give you room to escape if needed.

questions.question: If your rear wheel locks while stopping on a straight road:

options.text: You can usually keep control of the motorcycle.
You will likely lose control of the motorcycle.
You must release the rear brake to regain control.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can usually keep control of the motorcycle.
questions.explanation: If your rear wheel locks while you stop on a straight road, keep it locked until you stop. You can control your motorcycle even with a locked rear wheel if you are upright and going straight.

questions.question: Which of these is a slippery surface?
questions.explanation: Surfaces with poor grip include wet, snowy, icy, or muddy pavement; gravel roads; lane markings; and metal covers on the road.

questions.question: To avoid confusing other drivers, you should:

options.text: Keep a longer distance behind other vehicles.
Turn off your turn signal after completing a turn or lane change.
Use your horn only in emergencies.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn off your turn signal after completing a turn or lane change.
questions.explanation: Turn off your turn signal after you finish turning or changing lanes. Leaving it on confuses other drivers.

questions.question: When should you inspect your motorcycle for safety?
questions.explanation: Always inspect your motorcycle before you ride. A small problem on a motorcycle is more dangerous than a small problem on a car.

questions.question: How should you brake?
questions.explanation: Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: When riding during the day, you should wear:
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen during the day. Wear clothing with reflective material so other drivers can see you better. Always wear clothing that covers your arms and legs.

questions.question: When you reach an uncontrolled intersection at the same time as another vehicle:

options.text: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
Flash your headlight to signal the other vehicle to go.
Continue through and expect the other vehicle to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
questions.explanation: At an uncontrolled intersection with no signs or traffic lights, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right.

questions.question: When motorcyclists ride in a group:

options.text: Inexperienced riders should lead the group.
Inexperienced riders should ride near the front.
Inexperienced riders should ride at the back.

questions.correctAnswerText: Inexperienced riders should ride near the front.
questions.explanation: Less experienced riders should ride near the front of the group, right behind the leader. This way, experienced riders can lead and watch the less experienced riders.

questions.question: When it starts to rain, it is usually best to:

options.text: Ride in the center of the lane.
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
Stop at the side of the road until the rain stops.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: When it rains, the center of the lane becomes slippery with oil. Ride in the tire tracks left by cars instead. The left tire track is often safest.

questions.question: As your motorcycle speeds up, you will:

options.text: Need to shift up through the gears.
Need to shift down through the gears.
Need to put the motorcycle in neutral.

questions.correctAnswerText: Need to shift up through the gears.
questions.explanation: You must shift into higher gears as your motorcycle speeds up.

questions.question: A motorcycle's horn is ________ a car's horn.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle's horn is quieter than a car's horn. Use your horn when needed, but do not rely on it to keep you safe.

questions.question: As you drink more alcohol, your ability to ride safely:
questions.explanation: Your riding skills get worse as you drink more alcohol. If you have had any alcohol, do not ride your motorcycle.

questions.question: When stopping, you should:
questions.explanation: Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop. Using both brakes helps you stop quickly and safely.

questions.question: When riding during the day, you should:

options.text: Wear dark clothes since it is bright outside.
Wear bright clothes so drivers can see you.
Wear shorts if it is hot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear bright clothes so drivers can see you.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen during the day. Wear bright-colored clothing when riding to make yourself more visible to other drivers.

questions.question: Increase your following distance if:
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance when your motorcycle takes longer to stop, when you cannot see ahead clearly, or when traffic is heavy.
